title: Syriana
events_chronological: Bob Barnes, a career field officer, sells two missiles in Tehran and loses track of one of them, which an arms dealer takes away.
In a Gulf emirate the drilling rights held by the oil company Connex are handed instead to a Chinese firm.
Wasim, a migrant worker on the emirate's oilfield, is laid off with his father when the contract changes hands.
Connex announces a merger with a small company, Killen, which has just won the drilling rights in Kazakhstan.
A government inquiry opens into the merger, and the lawyer Bennett Holiday is told to find exactly enough corruption to satisfy it.
The energy analyst Bryan Woodman brings his family to a party at the Emir's palace, where his small son is electrocuted in the pool.
Prince Nasir, the Emir's elder son, hires Woodman as an adviser out of guilt and out of conviction.
Wasim and his father queue for work and are drawn into a school where a preacher takes a close interest in them.
Barnes is sent to Beirut to arrange the killing of Prince Nasir, who is judged unfriendly to American interests.
Barnes is betrayed to a militia, tortured, dumped, and comes home to find himself under suspicion by his own service.
Nasir sets out his programme to Woodman: the rights go to the highest bidder, the parliament gets teeth, and women get the vote.
Holiday finds that an executive at Killen paid bribes for the Kazakh field, and delivers him to the inquiry along with his own mentor.
The Emir names his younger son rather than Nasir as his successor.
Barnes works out that the assassination is going ahead anyway and drives into the desert to warn Nasir.
Wasim and another young man take the missing missile out to sea in a fishing boat.
A missile from a drone destroys Nasir's convoy in the desert, killing Nasir, his family, Woodman's employer and Barnes.
Wasim drives the boat into the side of a new Connex-Killen tanker and the missile detonates.
The merger is approved, and the men who arranged all of it are photographed receiving an award.
syuzhet_notes: Four strands are cut into one another from the first reel with almost no captions, and none of them is a flashback: they are simply happening at once in different countries and converge on the same fortnight.
fabula_notes: The ordering follows the causal chain from the lost missile and the transferred drilling rights. Concurrent strands can be ranked either way.
